messages.subject: dataProcess function
messages.body_plain:
MSstats team,

I am using MSstats to process DIA data exported from Skyline. I am using the R script you provided at the summer school as a starting point.
As far as I can tell, things run smoothly until the point where the dataProcess function is called. R then gets stuck with :

"== Start the summarization per subplot...
  |========                                                              |  11%"

What is the expected timeframe of this function and is there a way to increase the speed of this step?I have a reasonable number of proteins/peptides (see attached the msstats.log), however I have many biological replicates (>50) which might explain why this step is slow.

Thanks for the help,
Franziska

messages.subject: Re: TechRepMixture & Fraction in the annotation file
messages.subject_clean: TechRepMixture & Fraction in the annotation file
messages.body_plain:
Hi Matthias,

The meaning of Mixture, TechRepMixture and Fraction are as follows:
Mixture: Mixture of samples labeled with different TMT reagents, which can be analyzed in a single mass spectrometry experiment.
TechRepMixture: Technical replicate ID of one mixture. One mixture may have multiple technical replicates. For example, if there are two technical replicates of one mixture (such as Mixture1), then TechRepMixture = "1" or "2" and Mixture = "Mixture1".
Fraction: Fraction ID. One technical replicate of one mixture may be fractionated into multiple fractions to increase the analytical depth. Then one technical replicate of one mixture should correspond to multiple fractions. For example, if the first technical replicate of one mixture (such as Mixture1) has three fractions, then Fraction = "1" or "2" or "3",  TechRepMixture= "1",  Mixture = "Mixture1".
BioReplicate : Unique ID for biological subject. If the channel doesn’t have sample, please add ’Empty’ under BioReplicate.
Best,
Ting
